sense: hopeful, confident that things will go well

terms.gloss: to be of good heart, to be positive
terms.grammar: phrase: bonō animō es! be positive, cheer up
evidence: Cic. Att. 5.18.3: quā rē bonō animō es
terms.comment: Also bonum animum habēre (Plaut. Capt. 152), and in a letter, just bonum animum (Cic. Att. 16.12.1). To someone downcast, Bonō animō es! (see cheer up).

terms.gloss: to be hopeful, to expect the best
evidence: Nep. Milt. 1.1: dē eō bene spērāre (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: positive (in grammar); laid down by convention
evidence: Gell. 10.4 lemma: nōmina nōn positīva esse sed nātūrālia (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 232, 246, 248: gradus positīvus, the positive degree
terms.comment: A term of grammar, the positive degree (gradus positīvus), or of words fixed by convention rather than by nature (Gellius); in Gauss, a positive number (Morgan–Owens). Never “hopeful”.

phrases.latin: tamen magnō timōre sum sed bene spērāmus
phrases.english: all the same, I am very anxious; but we are hopeful

phrases.latin: sed quid tibi dīcam? bonum animum.
phrases.english: but what am I to say to you? Keep your spirits up.

phrases.latin: Bonō animō es: dūcēs uxōrem hanc. — Hem. — Bonō animō es, inquam.
phrases.english: Cheer up: you’ll marry her. — What? — Cheer up, I tell you.

sources: Lewis & Short: animus · Lewis & Short: spero · Lewis & Short: positivus
